# Spec — #557: Guardian edge TLS guide + client-side HTTPS refusal for plain-HTTP remote targets

> **HISTORICAL:** Pre-RC implementation snapshot. Its separate-client and
> official hosted-origin assumptions were superseded. Current authority is
> `docs/technical/architecture.md` and `docs/remote-access-tls.md`.

_Milestone 0.13.0, Phase 3, task 5. Written 2026-07-12 against the current branch
(0.13.0-beta.3 baseline + merged #490, #433, #435, #488). Source assessment:
[`../assessments/557.md`](../assessments/557.md). Key claims re-verified against
the working tree: the CORS half is fully shipped
(`packages/guardian/src/config.ts:30-63` exact-origin allowlist rejecting `*`,
`packages/guardian/src/cors.test.ts` 9-case subprocess suite,
`portals.compose.yml:132` local-client-origins default pinned by
`packages/lib/src/control-plane/assistant-client-compose.test.ts:195-220`,
client-side `blocked`/`cors` probe state + remediation copy pinned by
`packages/client/tests/transport-health-cors.test.ts` and
`tests/connections-page-markup.test.ts`); `requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections`
has ZERO consumers (`packages/ui/src/lib/server/features.ts:130`;
`docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes.md:112-117` says "policy, not yet
enforcement"); `isLoopbackHost` exists but is module-private
(`packages/client/src/lib/connections/index.ts:54`); no TLS guide or
tailscale/caddy reference exists anywhere under `docs/` (grep-verified —
only roadmap/plan/review docs mention them); the add/edit form URL placeholder
is a plain-HTTP LAN URL (`+page.svelte:383`); `/connections/new` is a
redirect alias with no form of its own (`new/+page.svelte`); #435's mTLS on
the direct listener and #488's host mDNS responder have already merged on this
branch, so both are coordination-notes-only here._

## 0. Decisions recorded (the assessment's open calls)

### D1 — Refusal trigger: the client refuses a plain-HTTP non-loopback target **iff the app itself runs on an `https:` origin**. Not the assessment's broader "https or non-loopback origin".

The assessment sketch ("rejects http:// URLs whose hostname is non-loopback
when the app itself runs on an https **or non-loopback** origin") is
over-eager, and its own risk list says so ("an over-eager check would regress
the zero-TLS desktop default"). The "or non-loopback origin" half would break
a **shipped, working** path: the assistant-container client served on a LAN IP
(`http://192.168.x.x:3810`) whose locked seeded connection is rewritten to the
visited LAN hostname (`rewriteLoopbackUrlForBrowserHost`,
`connections/index.ts:58-69`) — origin non-loopback `http:`, target
non-loopback `http:`, **not** mixed content, works in every browser today. A
probe short-circuit there would brand a healthy shipped connection "needs
HTTPS".

The `https:`-origin rule is exactly the platform rule the issue cites (mixed
content: "an HTTPS origin cannot `fetch()` a plain-HTTP guardian") and exactly
the issue's own wording ("the **hosted client** refuses plain-HTTP
non-loopback targets"). It preserves both legitimate plain-HTTP tiers named in
the risk list:

- loopback **targets** from any origin — allowed (browsers treat
  `http://127.0.0.1` as potentially trustworthy; mixed-content exempt);
- plain-HTTP LAN guardians from a **loopback-origin** client (the zero-TLS
  desktop default) — allowed (a `http://127.0.0.1` origin is a secure context
  with no mixed-content restriction);
- plus the LAN-served client tier above.

The residual adjacency (a LAN-served plain-HTTP client sending Basic auth over
HTTP — review E7/I3) is explicitly out of scope here and recorded in § 7 so
this issue is not misread as resolving it.

### D2 — Hosted origin (`https://app.openpalm.dev`) is NOT baked into the compose CORS default. Operator-opt-in until #511's hosted deploy exists.

This ratifies the implementation plan's cross-cutting decision
(implementation-plan.md:152-153: "enters the compose CORS default only when
the hosted deploy actually exists") and the assessment's risk 1: review
finding I4 was fixed by defaulting the allowlist to LOCAL client origins only,
and `GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS` still defaults to `false`; pre-baking a
not-yet-existing origin into every install widens the browser-reachable
surface for zero benefit. The decision is **pinned by a test** (§ 2.4) so a
future "helpful" addition is a deliberate act under #511, and the TLS guide
documents the one-line `stack.env` override for when the hosted client (or any
custom origin) is used. `portals.compose.yml` is therefore **unchanged** by
this task, and the guardian CORS test suite needs no additions (the
assessment's own conclusion).

### D3 — TLS integration ships as a guided doc with copy-paste `custom.compose.yml` snippets. No managed tailscale/caddy compose overlay in `packages/skeleton/`.

The issue marks the sidecar as optional ("(optionally) a sidecar/serve
integration"). Reasons to keep it docs-only, recorded for the issue close-out:

1. **External infrastructure either way.** A Tailscale sidecar needs a
   tailnet account and a `TS_AUTHKEY` secret; Caddy DNS-challenge needs a
   user-owned domain, a DNS provider API token, and a **per-provider Caddy
   plugin build** (the stock `caddy` image ships no DNS-provider modules — a
   managed overlay would have to pick providers or make users build images).
   Neither can be smoke-tested in CI; both are "verifiable only by manual
   smoke" (assessment test strategy).
2. **The sanctioned extension point already fits.** Custom services belong in
   the user-owned `config/stack/custom.compose.yml` (core-principles § 1b) —
   the same pattern #435's spec chose for mTLS secret grants (D4 there). The
   simplest Tailscale path doesn't even need a container: `tailscale serve`
   on the host, fronting the already-published `127.0.0.1:3830`.
3. **Scope discipline** (assessment risk 3): a managed overlay drags in
   rootless-container and image-pinning work and would balloon the task past M.

The guide ships exact, complete snippets (host-mode `tailscale serve`
one-liner as the recommended default; a `custom.compose.yml` Caddy service +
file-dropped `Caddyfile` as the alternative), so the flow is still guided —
"TLS is never a manual user task on default paths" is satisfied because the
default paths (desktop/localhost) need no TLS at all, and the remote path is
copy-paste with a real Let's Encrypt cert on both routes (no private CA ever).

### D4 — Guide location and deep link: `docs/remote-access-tls.md`, deep-linked as a pinned constant `TLS_GUIDE_URL`.

User-facing operational guides live at `docs/` top level (`setup-guide.md`,
`troubleshooting.md`, `password-management.md`); `docs/operations/` is
runbook/release territory. The client is a static artifact with no docs of its
own, so the deep link is the canonical GitHub URL:
`https://github.com/itlackey/openpalm/blob/main/docs/remote-access-tls.md`
(repo URL verified from `packages/client/package.json`). The constant lives in
the new `url-policy.ts` module and a test pins that the path segment named by
the constant exists in the repo (§ 2.3), so a doc rename breaks CI instead of
shipping a dead link. Stable H2 anchors: `## Tailscale (recommended)` and
`## Caddy with your own domain`.

### D5 — `requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections` stays a host-side declaration; enforcement is computed client-locally from the app origin.

`packages/client` NEVER depends on `@openpalm/lib` or host APIs (purity gate,
`tests/purity.test.ts`), and the flag lives in the host UI's server runtime
context (`packages/ui/src/lib/server/features.ts:130`) which the static client
cannot and must not read. The enforcement condition (D1: app origin is
`https:`) is the client-local computation of the same policy — an https origin
IS the hosted/remote-install case the flag describes. `features.ts` is
therefore **unchanged**; `ui-runtime-modes.md` is updated to say the policy is
now enforced client-locally (origin-derived) and to stop calling the flag
consumer-less in spirit (the flag remains the host contract's declaration,
available to #511's `/api/runtime` handshake).

### D6 — Probe short-circuit: additive `'insecure'` health state, zero network I/O.

`probeHealth()` gains a pre-fetch check: if `validateConnectionUrl(base)`
refuses with `insecure-remote`, return
`{ state: 'insecure', detail: 'plain-http-remote' }` without calling `fetch`.
Today this case surfaces as `TypeError` → no-cors re-probe (**also**
mixed-content-blocked on an https origin) → misleading `unreachable`. The new
state is additive exactly like `'blocked'` was (existing consumers matching
the old vocabulary keep working). The validator lives in a new leaf module
`connections/url-policy.ts` so the transport does not import the IndexedDB
store module; `connections/index.ts` re-uses `isLoopbackHost` from it (moved,
not duplicated).

### D7 — #488/#435 coordination: documented in the guide, nothing built.

- **#488 (merged):** the host mDNS responder advertises plain-HTTP `.local`
  names for LAN discovery. The guide notes that a TLS-fronted guardian is
  reached by its `ts.net`/domain name, not the `.local` name — share the HTTPS
  URL with remote clients; mDNS stays the LAN-local affordance.
- **#435 (merged):** the direct listener (3830) optionally terminates **mTLS**
  as an adapter transport identity (`docs/technical/guardian-direct-mtls.md`).
  An edge TLS front for browsers proxies plain HTTP to `127.0.0.1:3830`, so
  the two features are **mutually exclusive on the same listener**: with mTLS
  enabled, the browser edge cannot front 3830 (the proxy holds no client
  cert). The guide states this explicitly and points operators wanting both at
  the mTLS design note's Caddy client-cert discussion (#435 spec D6).
- The client-side refusal is this issue's implementation of #435's
  "credentials only ever sent over HTTPS for non-loopback targets" clause for
  the hosted client: the add/edit form and the probe refuse the connection
  before any credentialed request exists (and on an https origin the browser's
  mixed-content blocker is the backstop — the request never leaves).

## 1. Scope

Closes these remaining-work items from the assessment:

1. **User-facing TLS guide** — `docs/remote-access-tls.md` per D3/D4:
   Tailscale `serve` default, Caddy alternative, exact env knobs
   (`GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS=true`, `GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` addition),
   private-CA non-goal, stable anchors.
2. **Client-side HTTPS enforcement** (the `requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections`
   consumer, per D1/D5/D6): `validateConnectionUrl()` in
   `packages/client/src/lib/connections/url-policy.ts`, wired into the
   `/connections` add/edit form with an actionable error deep-linking the
   guide, the `probeHealth()` short-circuit with matching remediation UI, and
   the plain-HTTP placeholder replaced.
3. **Hosted-origin allowlist decision** — decided (D2: keep operator-opt-in,
   trail #511), pinned by test, documented.
4. **Tests for the new enforcement** — § 2 (client unit + source-pin suites
   modeled on `transport-health-cors.test.ts` /
   `connections-page-markup.test.ts`; lib compose pin).
5. **Coordination hooks documented** (#488, #435) — per D7, guide + docs text
   only.
6. **`docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes.md` flip** — Security Boundaries
   paragraph rewritten from "policy, not yet enforcement" to enforced; the two
   #557 bullets removed from "Not Yet Shipped".

### Descoped (with justification)

- **Tailscale/Caddy compose overlay in `packages/skeleton/system/stack/`.**
  Per D3: the issue marks it optional; both routes need external
  infrastructure (tailnet auth key / owned domain + DNS API token +
  per-provider Caddy plugin image) that CI cannot exercise; the user-owned
  `custom.compose.yml` file-drop is the sanctioned extension point and the
  guide ships complete snippets. Recorded as the scoping decision the
  assessment asks for (issue close-out note § 8).
- **Baking `https://app.openpalm.dev` into the compose CORS default.** Per D2:
  deliberate security-posture decision, trails #511's actual hosted deploy;
  pinned by test so revisiting it is explicit.
- **Playwright e2e extension (`e2e/connections-form.pw.ts`).** The e2e preview
  server runs on a loopback origin, where D1's refusal deliberately never
  triggers — a form-refusal e2e cannot exercise the branch without faking the
  page origin, which Playwright cannot do honestly for `location.protocol`.
  The refusal is pure TS validated by unit tests plus source pins; the
  existing e2e (loopback URL fills) stays green as the no-regression proof for
  the allowed tier.
- **Refusal/warning UX for the LAN-served plain-HTTP client sending Basic
  auth over HTTP** (review E7/I3 adjacency, assessment risk 5). Not this
  issue's clause (the issue scopes refusal to the hosted client); changing the
  LAN tier's behavior belongs to #563's network-preset framing. Recorded in
  § 7 so the gap stays visible.
- **Guardian-side changes of any kind.** The CORS half is shipped and the
  default allowlist is unchanged (D2), so `packages/guardian` and
  `portals.compose.yml` are untouched; the guardian CORS suite needs no
  additions (assessment's own conclusion).
- **`features.ts` changes.** Per D5 — the flag is already computed and typed;
  its enforcement is client-local by architecture.

## 2. TEST-FIRST PLAN

All new tests are `bun:test` files under `packages/client/tests/`, run by
`bun run client:test` (`bun test --cwd packages/client`). Idioms to mirror:
injectable-fetch transport tests (`tests/transport-health-cors.test.ts`),
`globalThis.location` stubbing via a save/restore helper
(`tests/connections-seed.test.ts:34-48` `withLocationHost` — extend the stub
shape to `{ protocol, hostname }`), and static source/doc pins
(`tests/connections-page-markup.test.ts` — `readFileSync` + regex against the
`.svelte` source, the house pattern because packages/client has no
component-render harness). The lib pin extends the existing
`assistant-client-compose.test.ts` I4 describe block.

## 3. File-level changes

### Create

1. **`docs/remote-access-tls.md`** — the user-facing guide. Required content
   (order and anchors fixed; pinned by § 2.3):
   - **Why TLS is unavoidable for phones/remote clients** — secure-context and
     mixed-content platform rules, verbatim framing from the issue; the
     desktop/localhost path needs none of this (loopback origin tier).
   - **What you are exposing** — the guardian **direct listener**
     (`127.0.0.1:3830` by default; `portals.compose.yml:155` publishes
     `${OP_BIND_ADDRESS:-127.0.0.1}:${OP_GUARDIAN_PORT:-3830}:3830`), which
     404s everything until `GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS=true` (in
     `knowledge/env/stack.env`); loopback-default posture is unchanged — both
     routes below tunnel to loopback rather than opening a LAN/WAN bind.
   - **`## Tailscale (recommended)`** — host-mode `tailscale serve` fronting
     `http://127.0.0.1:3830` (e.g. `tailscale serve --bg 127.0.0.1:3830`),
     yielding `https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net` with an automatic Let's
     Encrypt cert (`tailscale cert` / HTTPS must be enabled on the tailnet);
     no cert management, no port forwarding, reachable only inside the
     tailnet. Steps: enable direct ingress → serve → add the **client app's
     origin** to `GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` → `docker compose up -d
     guardian` (or the admin UI apply). Note for container-only hosts: a
     `tailscale` sidecar in `config/stack/custom.compose.yml` with
     `TS_AUTHKEY` as a file secret is possible; snippet provided, marked
     advanced.
   - **`## Caddy with your own domain`** — for users who don't want Tailscale:
     Caddy reverse-proxying `127.0.0.1:3830` with a user-owned domain and
     DNS-challenge Let's Encrypt (works without opening port 80/443 to the
     internet if DNS-challenge is used with a LAN-only A record). Complete
     `custom.compose.yml` service block + file-dropped `Caddyfile` snippet;
     honest note that DNS-challenge needs a provider-specific Caddy build
     (link `caddy-dns` org) — which is exactly why this is the alternative,
     not the default.
   - **CORS origin note** (assessment risk 4): what goes in
     `GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is the **browser app's origin** (where
     the client is served from — e.g. the hosted client origin, or the
     `https://….ts.net` origin if you serve the client build through the same
     front), exact origins only, comma-separated, guardian rejects `*`;
     https origins are supported by the exact-origin matcher
     (`config.ts:30-40` normalizes via `URL.origin`; the CORS suite's allowed
     origin is literally `https://app.openpalm.dev`).
   - **Client behavior** — the client refuses plain-HTTP non-loopback targets
     when it runs on an https origin (this guide is where its error links);
     what the `needs HTTPS` badge means.
   - **Coordination notes (D7)** — mDNS `.local` names are LAN/plain-HTTP
     affordances (#488); mTLS on 3830 and a browser TLS front are mutually
     exclusive on the same listener (#435, link
     `docs/technical/guardian-direct-mtls.md`).
   - **Non-goals** — no private-CA installs on iOS/Android (mkcert-style),
     ever; no public-internet exposure guidance beyond these two paths.

2. **`packages/client/src/lib/connections/url-policy.ts`** — leaf module,
   zero imports (purity-safe by construction):

   ```ts
   export const TLS_GUIDE_URL =
     'https://github.com/itlackey/openpalm/blob/main/docs/remote-access-tls.md';

   export function isLoopbackHost(hostname: string): boolean; // moved verbatim from index.ts:54-56

   export type ConnectionUrlVerdict =
     | { ok: true }
     | { ok: false; reason: 'invalid-url'; message: string }
     | { ok: false; reason: 'insecure-remote'; message: string; guideUrl: string };

   /**
    * D1: refuse plain-http non-loopback targets iff the app origin is https:
    * (mixed content — the request could never succeed; refuse with guidance
    * instead of a generic fetch failure). origin defaults to
    * globalThis.location; null/undefined origin ⇒ ok (non-browser context).
    */
   export function validateConnectionUrl(
     rawUrl: string,
     origin: { protocol: string; hostname: string } | null = globalThis.location ?? null
   ): ConnectionUrlVerdict;
   ```

   Implementation: `new URL(rawUrl)` (throw ⇒ `invalid-url`); protocol must be
   `http:`/`https:` (else `invalid-url`); `https:` target ⇒ ok; `http:` +
   loopback target ⇒ ok; `http:` + non-loopback target ⇒ refuse only when
   `origin?.protocol === 'https:'`, with a message naming HTTPS and the guide
   (`guideUrl: TLS_GUIDE_URL`). No `any`; strict narrowing throughout.

3. **`packages/client/tests/connections-url-policy.test.ts`**,
   **`packages/client/tests/transport-health-insecure.test.ts`**,
   **`packages/client/tests/connections-https-refusal.test.ts`** — § 2.

| Issue acceptance criterion | Proof |
|---|---|
| "Recommended default: Tailscale. Guided docs + (optionally) a sidecar/serve integration" | Guide `## Tailscale (recommended)` with complete steps (§ 3.1); optional sidecar consciously scoped to a documented `custom.compose.yml` snippet (D3, recorded on the issue); § 2.3 doc pins |
| "Alternative: Caddy front … user-owned domain (DNS-challenge Let's Encrypt)" | Guide `## Caddy with your own domain` + snippet; § 2.3 anchor pin |
| "CORS allowlist on guardian ingress … enforced tests" | Already shipped (verified: `config.ts:30-63`, `server.ts` preflight handling, `cors.test.ts` 9-case suite) — no change needed; still green in the guardian gate |
| "official hosted origin (e.g. app.openpalm.dev) baked in" | **Decided against for now** (D2, ratifies implementation-plan cross-cutting decision); § 2.4 pin records it; guide documents the one-line override; trails #511 |
| "additional origins configurable" | Shipped (`GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` override, `portals.compose.yml:132`); guide + `environment-and-mounts.md` tell TLS users exactly which origin to add |
| "`requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections` enforced client-side too: the hosted client refuses plain-HTTP non-loopback targets with an actionable message deep-linking to the TLS guide" | § 2.1 refusal tests, § 2.2 probe short-circuit tests, § 2.3 form/badge/deep-link source pins; the guide file exists at the pinned URL path |
| "Coordinate with #488 (mDNS … HTTPS name) and #435 (credentials only ever sent over HTTPS for non-loopback targets)" | D7: guide coordination section (§ 2.3 mTLS pin); refusal-at-form + probe implements the #435 clause for the hosted client; both features already merged, nothing built here |
| Non-goal: "No change to the loopback-default posture" | Zero compose/guardian changes; §2.2 pins that loopback-origin and loopback-target plain-HTTP paths stay allowed; existing guardian + client suites green |
| Non-goal: no private-CA on phones | Guide non-goals section; § 2.3 pin |
| Simplicity guardrail: "TLS is never a manual user task on default paths" | Default (loopback) paths need no TLS and are untouched; remote path is guided copy-paste with automatic Let's Encrypt on both routes (D3) |

## 5. Verification gates (implementer must run green)

- `bun run lint`
- `bun run check`
- `bun run client:build && bun run client:test` (build first — the purity
  dist-grep fails loudly on a missing build)
- `cd packages/guardian && bun test --no-orphans` (must match the pre-change
  baseline — this task changes nothing in guardian)
- **Additionally for this task** (§ 2.4 lives in lib): `bun run lib:test` —
  compared against the pre-change baseline for the known sandbox root-uid
  flakes only.

## 6. Risks and how the design avoids them

1. **Baked-in hosted origin conflicts with the I4 security posture**
   (assessment risk 1): resolved by D2 — not baked in, pinned by § 2.4, guide
   documents the opt-in; revisit under #511 with the deploy in hand.
2. **Over-eager refusal regresses legitimate plain-HTTP paths** (risk 2): D1
   scopes the trigger to https origins only — the exact mixed-content rule.
   Both preserved tiers (loopback-origin desktop default, LAN-served client)
   have dedicated allow tests (§ 2.1/§ 2.2) so a future "tightening" must
   consciously delete a pin. The e2e suite's loopback fills double as a
   browser-level no-regression check.
3. **Sidecar integration balloons the task** (risk 3): D3 — docs-only with
   copy-paste `custom.compose.yml` snippets in the user-owned overlay; zero
   managed-compose changes; recorded scoping decision for the issue.
4. **TLS front changes the Origin the guardian matches** (risk 4): verified —
   the exact-origin matcher normalizes via `URL.origin` and handles https
   origins (the CORS suite's allowed origin is `https://app.openpalm.dev`
   already); the guide's CORS note tells users to allowlist the browser app's
   https origin explicitly.
5. **Issue misread as resolving the LAN plain-HTTP credentials exposure**
   (risk 5, review E7/I3): explicitly descoped with a pointer (§ 1, § 7) and
   the D1 rationale documents why the LAN tier stays allowed; ui-runtime-modes
   keeps describing that tier honestly.
6. **Dead deep link after a docs reshuffle** (spec-added): the § 2.3 pin ties
   `TLS_GUIDE_URL`'s path segment to a real file; a rename breaks CI.
7. **Purity regression via new imports** (spec-added): `url-policy.ts` is a
   zero-import leaf; the purity dist-grep gate runs in `client:test` after
   `client:build`.

## 7. Out of scope

- Tailscale/Caddy managed compose overlay or any `packages/skeleton` change
  (D3; snippets live in the guide, services in the user overlay).
- `https://app.openpalm.dev` in the default CORS allowlist; the hosted deploy
  itself; `/api/runtime` handshake; pairing/QR (all #511).
- Warning/refusal UX for the LAN-served plain-HTTP client tier and its
  IndexedDB-credential exposure (review E7/I3 — revisit under #563's presets).
- Per-request credential-attach enforcement inside the transport `request()`
  path (the form + probe + browser mixed-content blocker cover the surface;
  revisit only if a non-form path to insecure entries appears).
- Any guardian code change: TLS termination in the guardian process
  (server-only TLS was explicitly assigned to the edge by #435's D3), CORS
  parser changes, new listeners.
- Playwright e2e for the refusal (loopback-origin harness cannot trigger it
  honestly — § 1 descope).
- mDNS advertising HTTPS names (#488 follow-up if ever needed; the guide
  documents the manual expectation instead).
- `features.ts` / host-UI changes (D5).
